result.verdict: Postable after small edits; no hard rule violation. Rule 1 passes: no drive or docs.google links, and no matching tokens. The session id's alphanumeric part is 24 characters and post.sh exempts 'session_' tokens. Rule 2 passes: no Grok, version or other model identifiers. 'Anthropic Claude' is borderline (nit). Rule 3: one bare 'main#454'. It is same-repo so it cannot mislink, but it should be an explicit link. Rule 4 passes: no closing verbs before #N. Rule 5 passes: no independence credit claimed, 'scientific effect NONE' and 'No status change' are both stated, and 'Credit 0' could name the credit. Rule 6 passes: I checked all three links against the GitHub REST API. Verdict 6282139686 is a cursor[bot] comment at pull/454. Pickup 6282034959 is at pull/454. Record 6280394188 is at issues/419. Each link uses the right form. The main issues are rule 7 clarity: '024 l.74', '§12 §2(b)', 'this record' (meaning this comment), 'not logged in the unit', and two unclear '48-angle' or factor phrases. Separately, the finite-r ±0.001 claim on line 12 is over-precise according to cursor/num/finite_r.log. I wrote nothing to scratch and posted nothing.

The draft is accurate on substance, but it needs changes before posting: one numeric overclaim, several statements that verification was broader than it was, and one attribution that misleads. The numbers I recomputed match the logs. The closed form gives 3.2309785. The r→0 limits are 0.2200–0.2205 and 0.4784–0.4794 with 96–192 midpoints. The adversarial pass gives 0.0999, 0.0538 and 0.0272 at t = r^(2/3). The growth factors are 16.21 and 16.05. Line 70 of bfcheck.py is a rule with 8 midpoints on (0, π) (nodes at 11.25° to 168.75°), weighted by 2π/8. Problems: (1) the ±0.001 band is said to hold at finite r from 0.04, but the r = 0.04 values are 0.2176 and 0.4825. (2) "Three separate readers" is too strong: the adversarial pass read the numeric pass's profile log while both were running, and the numeric pass reused the record's bfcheck.py functions. (3) Several checks are presented as general when only one pass did them: the power-count reruns and the r^(2/3) integral (adversarial only), and the finite-r runs to r = 0.005 (numeric only). (4) The verdict only cleared the three statements the request named, not all of the record's "other §2(b) statements". (5) "Every … equation attribution matches" contradicts the draft's own small points. (6) "Not logged in the unit" rests on the adversarial pass searching the numeric pass's scratch folder; the verdict never said the figure was logged anywhere. The correction does not overstate the 0.42 error. It slightly understates the estimator defect: the matching 0.22 at t = 0.2 comes from the same 8-node grid and agrees only by where the nodes fall. It also leaves out that the verdict itself flagged the 0.42. Nothing the checkers listed as a correction is missing from the draft. I wrote no files.
